quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and keep your speed.
Speed up to leave the area quickly.

questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who may cross in front of you. If you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: As blood alcohol concentration (BAC) goes up, you become:
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the amount of alcohol in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you become.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.

questions.explanation: Always signal before you change lanes to tell other drivers. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving your vehicle left or right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign warns you that traffic is merging from the right. Be ready to let the traffic merge safely.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, you should:

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell.

questions.explanation: Do not take road rage personally. If another driver cuts you off, ignore it and keep driving safely.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle uses sirens and flashing lights, you should pull to the right side of the road and let it pass.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and sirens on, move to the right side of the road right away and let it pass.

questions.question: What can happen when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: The effects of both may get stronger.
The effects of both may get weaker.
Only the alcohol's effects may get weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both may get stronger.
questions.explanation: Alcohol combined with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, drinking one beer while using a cold medicine can affect you like you drank several beers.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger tells you to stop.
A stop sign controls the crossing.
Flashing red signals and gates are working.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to. Also stop when flashing red signals and gates are operating.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in heavy traffic, keep moving slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: What does a "No standing" sign mean?

options.text: You can never stop your vehicle there.
You can park there if the driver stays in the vehicle.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you can only stop for a short time to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Always wear both the lap belt and the shoulder belt. Using only one part does not protect you well. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, also buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: Like alcohol and other drugs, drowsiness can:

options.text: Help you be a better driver.

questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep causes poor driving. Sleepiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and impairs judgment—just like drugs and alcohol.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should wait until the entire car is visible in your rearview mirror before moving back to the right lane.
questions.explanation: Do not return to your lane until you can see the entire vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: On a long trip, what is a good way to prevent fatigue?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours for a short break on long trips. If you feel drowsy, pull off the road safely and take a nap or find a place to stay for the night.

questions.question: The maximum posted speed limit should only be driven:
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest legal speed under ideal conditions. Drive at the same speed as other traffic, up to the limit. All drivers must maintain safe speeds.

questions.question: How can you prevent yourself from becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Drive above the posted speed limit.
Tailgate the driver in front of you.

questions.explanation: Concentrate on driving and don't take other drivers' actions personally. Be realistic about travel time, drive within speed limits, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: Pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections always have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way when crossing at an intersection. A crosswalk exists wherever two streets meet, whether marked or unmarked.

questions.question: In which ways can alcohol affect you?
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It slows reaction time, coordination, and balance. It also impairs your vision and ability to judge distance.

questions.question: Following too closely behind other drivers:

options.text: Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
Cannot result in a traffic citation.
Reduces collisions by preventing being cut off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
questions.explanation: Following too closely is dangerous and should be avoided. It can lead to aggressive driving and legal consequences.

questions.question: You may leave a collision scene if the damage does not look serious.
questions.explanation: Never leave a collision scene without taking proper steps. Leaving may result in prosecution for hit and run.
